question:
A DevOps engineer must use Python to manage a Cisco device. The device is in a highly secure DMZ environment. Only trusted Cisco Python libraries can be used.
Which solution meets the requirements?
options: Develop an on-box Python script that uses trusted Cisco libraries.
Develop an application by using serverless technologies in a primary cloud provider.
Develop an off-box Python script that uses trusted Cisco libraries.
Develop a containerization application that uses trusted Cisco-provided libraries.
theory: Running the automation directly on the device with NX-OS's embedded, on-box Python interpreter and Cisco's built-in cisco/cli Python packages keeps the entire toolchain within Cisco-provided, trusted code and avoids any external network path into the DMZ-isolated device. Off-box scripts, cloud-serverless functions, and generic containerized apps would all pull in non-Cisco runtimes/libraries and require reaching into the DMZ from outside, conflicting with the 'only trusted Cisco libraries' restriction. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 17 — Evaluate Automation and Orchestration Technologies)
